scenes.contextualRelevance: The focus on strumming as the key aspect of this particular lesson implies that mastering strumming patterns is crucial for playing even simple songs effectively.

narrativeProgression.description: The musician greets the audience and reveals the title of the song, 'Horse with No Name'.
He emphasizes that the song only has two chords used consistently throughout, making it an excellent opportunity to focus on strumming techniques.
He highlights the beauty of the song and its suitability for learning intricate strumming patterns like the Ed Sheeran style.

scenes.contextualRelevance: Clear instruction on chord and strumming techniques aids in understanding the song's structure and execution.

narrativeProgression.description: The musician introduces the first chord, E minor (Em), showing how to play it using two fingers.
He acknowledges different ways to play the chord, indicating flexibility in guitar techniques.
He demonstrates the second chord, D6add9/F#, emphasizing its simplicity despite its complex name.
He encourages using a third finger if the stretch for the D6add9/F# chord is difficult.
He emphasizes that all six strings should ring out for both chords.
He explains that the song structure involves playing a bar of each chord.
He demonstrates the simplest way to play a bar of each chord by strumming on the beat.
He acknowledges that the E minor chord can make the song sound sad but emphasizes the uplifting role of the strumming pattern.
He explains that each chord has a different strumming pattern applied to it.
He starts demonstrating the first bar's strumming pattern on the E minor chord.
He demonstrates the second bar's strumming pattern, emphasizing the change in rhythm with two upstrokes in a row.
He suggests practicing the strumming pattern on the E minor chord to focus on the pattern itself.
He offers a simplified version of the strumming pattern, replacing the root notes with downstrokes.
He encourages practicing both strumming patterns with and without root notes.
He recommends singing along with the 'la la la' part of the song's chorus to synchronize singing with the strumming.
